item: chaos coverage extended beyond search, to the store that holds the cart
not_deployed: disposable containers on random ports; no project volume or Compose service is touched
why_cart: The search drill asserts a Redis outage costs latency and not availability, because there Redis is a cache. Cart is the opposite and the more dangerous case: Redis holds the cart itself. CartService.getCart does findById(...).orElseGet(() -> new Cart(id)), where a miss legitimately means 'no cart yet'. If a connection failure were ever folded into that same path, a shopper with an intact cart would be shown an empty one, with 200 OK, no error, and nothing in any dashboard.

observations.after_recovery: the cart still held its item, with no restart

drill_result.note: This is the first verification of the cart-service Redis timeout added earlier the same day, which was recorded at the time as reasoned but not drill-verified.

defect_found_in_the_drill_itself: The first run reused whatever jar happened to be in target/, which predated the Redis timeout it was written to verify, and reported a 60-second stall as a property of the service rather than of the artifact. It now refuses a jar older than its source and asserts the timeout actually shipped in the packaged application.yml -- checking the property directly, because a 60-second stall has several possible causes and only one of them is the configuration.
supporting_tool: ops/testing/mint-access-token.py mints an RS256 access token with openssl and the standard library, so the drill can authenticate. Without it the drill could only reach /health, which reads no state at all.
limits: One service and one dependency. order-service against a failed PostgreSQL or Kafka, and the gateway's rate limiter against a stalled Redis, remain unexercised.
A paused container is a network black hole, which is one failure mode. Packet loss, slow responses and partial failures are not covered.
